title: Latency-cost opportunity map — KV cache & request-shape breakdown (draft)
content:
Summary:

This is a working draft of an "opportunity map" that correlates request shapes (seq len, prompt reuse, response length) with observed latency percentiles and incremental token cost. Purpose: provide the product + pricing teams with concrete buckets to target optimization (KV cache, batching, quantization, routing) and to give SRE/infra a prioritized list of tuning experiments.

High-level takeaway (short):
- Big wins (>30% cost or latency improvement) exist for workloads with high prefix reuse and short generation tails (common in chat assistants and code completion).
- Moderate wins (10–25%) from 4-bit quantization on long sequence workloads where KV memory pressure is primary.
- Little-to-no win (<5%) for one-offs with long, unpredictable prompts and long outputs unless we change routing to cheaper model variants.

Methodology / test harness notes:
- Test harness: local load generator calling hosted inference endpoint (stable model v2.3.1-serve) with realistic tokenization using tiktoken.
- Instances: A100-40GB (prod pool), H100-80GB (experimental), and cg7-small-8 (inference-optimized vCPU-backed cheaper tier).
- Configs: baseline = no-kvcache + dynamic batching (default). Experiments: kvcache enabled (prefix reuse ration 0.6–0.9), q4/4-bit static quant, force-batch-size=1, request-routes (fallback-to-small).
- Measurements: p50/p90/p99 latency (ms), tokens-per-second, cost-per-1k-output-tokens (USD) using internal pricing calculator. Each measurement run = 30k requests across 24 hours to capture diurnal variance.

Request-shape taxonomy used in tests:
1) ShortPrompt-ShortGen (S-S): prompt <= 128 tokens, generate <= 64 tokens, high prefix reuse (session chat).
2) ShortPrompt-LongGen (S-L): prompt <= 128 tokens, generate 512–1024 tokens (summarization without reuse).
3) LongPrompt-ShortGen (L-S): prompt 512–2048 tokens, generate <= 64 tokens (context-heavy retrieval Q&A).
4) OneOff-LongGen (O-L): one-off prompts 256–2048, generate 512–1024 tokens (creative generation).

Representative ASCII charts (median and tail deltas, numbers are illustrative from runs):

Latency p50/p90/p99 (ms) by request-shape, baseline vs kvcache-enabled (A100):

Shape    | baseline p50 / p90 / p99 | kvcache p50 / p90 / p99 | % p50 delta | % p99 delta
---------|--------------------------|--------------------------|-------------|----------
S-S      | 45 / 110 / 320           | 27 / 68 / 120            | -40%        | -62%     
S-L      | 62 / 220 / 840           | 58 / 210 / 790           | -6%         | -6%      
L-S      | 120 / 380 / 1200         | 78 / 230 / 640           | -35%        | -47%     
O-L      | 180 / 620 / 1800         | 178 / 610 / 1790         | -1%         | -0.6%    

Cost per 1k output tokens (USD) by request-shape, baseline vs kvcache-enabled (A100):

Shape    | baseline $/1k | kvcache $/1k | absolute delta | % improvement
---------|---------------|--------------|----------------|---------------
S-S      | 0.054         | 0.018        | -0.036         | -66%          
S-L      | 0.12          | 0.11         | -0.01          | -8%           
L-S      | 0.21          | 0.14         | -0.07          | -33%          
O-L      | 0.32          | 0.319        | -0.001         | -0.3%         

Interpretation / opportunities:
- S-S (chat-like) is the top-priority optimization target. High prefix reuse + short tails => huge KV cache hit rate and both latency and cost collapse. Product implication: encourage session-based usage, sticky session tokens, and session tokens in SDKs.
- L-S (context-heavy Q&A) also benefits strongly because large prompt prefix is reused between rephrases; optimizing KV eviction policy and chunking yields large wins.
- S-L and O-L see limited benefit from KV cache because generation is dominated by decode cost (large output tokens). For those, batching, quantization, or cheaper routing matter more.

Quantization sweep notes (A100 baseline, q8->q4):
- q8 (int8-like) gives 8–12% lower cost across all shapes with <5% p99 latency regression in long sequence runs.
- q4 (4-bit) yields 20–30% cost reduction for memory-bound L-S runs, but introduces ~10–18% p99 latency instability for O-L shapes due to extra kernel overheads; not recommended globally.

Routing and model-variant policy experiments (cheap-variant fallback):
- Small cheap-variant (lower-capacity float model) yields 25–40% cost reduction for O-L when semantic similarity of output requirement is low; p99 increases heavily (>2x) and quality regression observed in 15% of prompts. Good candidate for non-critical background tasks.

Opportunity map (prioritized actions):
1) KV cache SDK default: enable session KV cache for chat endpoints. Product + SDK change. Estimated potential hosted cost savings = 12–18% overall if 30% of calls are S-S.
2) KV eviction & chunking improvements: engineering project. Prioritize L-S pattern; potential per-cust savings >30% for retrieval apps.
3) Quantization profiles per workload: ship opt-in q4 for memory-bound dedicated pools; keep q8 for hosted baseline. Product gate and an opt-in toggle.
4) Routing policy: allow non-critical heavy-generation requests to route to cheaper variants with opt-out. Need quality monitoring and auto-backoff.

Open questions / unknowns:
- How representative are the prefix reuse ratios in production? We used session reuse 0.6–0.9; product telemetry is needed to validate.
- Interaction with autoscaling: high kvcache hit rates increase working set stability — but how does that affect GPU pod churn and tail-latency under noisy neighbours?
- Cost model assumptions: internal pricing used zero-overhead networking; need to include egress/IO ops for on-prem/private variants.

Quick reproducibility commands (dev notes):
- loadgen script: tools/loadgen/run.py --model v2.3.1-serve --shape S-S --rate 120 --duration 4h --kvcache on --quant q8
- measurement collector: tools/bench/collect_metrics.sh --job latency-cost --out runs/s-s-kv-20251102.csv
- compare script: tools/bench/compare.py runs/*.csv --metric p99 --format ascii-table

Next steps (practical):
- Ask Product to expose session-id in SDKs and make KV cache the default for chat endpoints (owner: Priya).
- Engineering spike: prototype dynamic KV chunking and eviction thresholds for L-S workloads (owner: Marcus). 3-week spike.
- Finance: run conservative projection model if 30% of traffic converts to session-enabled clients; estimate hosted margin change.

Notes to self: include real product telemetry before presenting this to pricing. Also run comparable experiments on H100 to check if cache benefits scale similarly with larger L2.
